title: SNAP transition reasons lead to distinct following-month food-security paths
source_unit: identified SIPP person, adjacent reference-month SNAP transition with a classified recorded reason and following-month food-security outcome

observations.period: 2024; classified SNAP no -> yes transition, recorded reason, following-month food security

denominator.unit: classified entry pairs with valid following-month RFOODS; reason-specific valid denominators vary

low_or_very_low_food_security.unit: percent; weighted share; Fay-BRR SE 3.82 pp; approximate 95% CI 18.64–33.60

observations.method: Classify adjacent-month SNAP entry reasons, retain valid following-month RFOODS=2/3 with AFOODS validity, and estimate with WPFINWGT and 240 Fay-BRR replicate weights.
observations.uncertainty: Reason categories are observed for only 217 of 437 entry pairs; food-security valid records are smaller and reason cells are selected. The following month is record order, not proof of benefit or bill timing.
observations.subgroup: Persons entering reported SNAP receipt with a valid classified reason and following-month food-security response.
observations.counterinterpretation: Food insecurity may reflect prior need, income, health, household composition, timing, or another shock rather than SNAP entry or its reason.

observations.period: 2024; classified SNAP yes -> no transition, recorded reason, following-month food security

denominator.unit: classified exit pairs with valid following-month RFOODS; reason-specific valid denominators vary

low_or_very_low_food_security.unit: percent; weighted share; Fay-BRR SE 3.51 pp; approximate 95% CI 11.99–25.74

observations.method: Classify adjacent-month SNAP exit reasons, retain valid following-month RFOODS=2/3 with AFOODS validity, and estimate with WPFINWGT and 240 Fay-BRR replicate weights.
observations.uncertainty: Reason categories are observed for only 188 of 387 exit pairs; food-security valid records are smaller and reason cells are selected. Exit does not identify restored security or income.
observations.subgroup: Persons exiting reported SNAP receipt with a valid classified reason and following-month food-security response.
observations.counterinterpretation: Exit may reflect income, renewal, family change, noncollection, reporting, or another shock; food security is not a direct measure of program adequacy.

related_sources.claim: The reader-facing finding supplies the reason-specific food-security cells and interpretation boundary.
The reproduction audit preserves row counts, matched pairs, hashes, and aggregate estimates.

reproduction_audit.result: Aggregate entry and exit food-security estimates and selected reason cells reproduced to the displayed precision; raw inputs remain outside the repository.
reproduction_audit.interpretation: This is a same-person adjacent-month descriptive route comparison, not a causal program, recovery, remedy, trust, or political-action estimate.

boundary: This is a Fay-BRR weighted descriptive comparison of recorded SNAP transition reasons and following-month food security. It does not establish notice, effort, benefit amount, gap days, causal program protection, household recovery, remedy, trust, political action, or geopolitical consequence. Classified reason and food-security universes are smaller than all transition universes.
